# Migrate the drag sensors to Pointer Events with pointer capture

## Context

Two defect classes measured this week both trace to the same foundation: the drag sensors are a mouse/touch-event, hit-testing-based design. (1) A pointer crossing an iframe pane starves the move stream and can swallow `pointerup`, leaving a session in `neo-is-dragging` forever — #17883, shielded in PR #17887 by making iframes hit-test-inert during a session. (2) A session whose `pointerup` is lost terminates never — observed surviving multiple later gestures. Both are symptoms of relying on hit-testing to keep receiving a gesture the sensor already owns.

The platform primitive that removes the class is **pointer capture**: `setPointerCapture(pointerId)` routes every subsequent pointer event to the capturing element until release — hit-testing bypassed entirely (iframes included), `pointerup`/`pointercancel` delivery guaranteed to the captor, implicit release built in.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs` — claims gestures via `testPathInclusion` (`:135`), installs a document-level `dragstart → preventDefault` for the gesture (`:162`/`:217`), stamps `body.neo-drag-active` (`:160`/`:215`); secondary-click/ctrl/meta gating lives here too.
- `src/main/draggable/sensor/Touch.mjs` — a separate sensor for the same job. Pointer Events unify mouse, touch, and pen: the migration plausibly collapses two sensors into one.
- `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs:424` — session cleanup half.
- The sensors' OUTPUT contract (`drag:start` / `drag:move` / `drag:end` synthetic events into the worker world) stays untouched — consumers, DragZones, the dock stack, and the #17885 native-drag partition gate never notice.

## The Fix

Replace the mouse/touch listeners with pointer listeners; on claiming a gesture, `setPointerCapture` on a stable capture target; translate to the existing synthetic vocabulary; release capture on end/cancel. Port the existing gating semantics verbatim (dragTargetClasses claim, primary-button/modifier checks, the native-`dragstart` suppression for claimed gestures, `neo-drag-active` stamping). Migration details that must not be lost:

- `touch-action: none` (or `pan-x`/`pan-y` as appropriate) on drag handles — without it, browser gestures fire `pointercancel` mid-drag on touch devices.
- `pointercancel` is a first-class terminal now: it must end sessions as cleanly as `pointerup` (this is the structural fix for the never-terminating session).
- The #17887 iframe shield stays in place as defense-in-depth; whether it can retire is a **later, evidence-gated** decision once capture has soaked (explicitly not part of this ticket).
- The #17885 partition contract (native-drag sources exempt from sensor claiming) applies unchanged to the new listeners.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One pointer-based sensor path drives mouse, touch, and pen; the synthetic `drag:*` contract is byte-compatible for consumers.
- [ ] A drag whose pointer crosses an iframe keeps streaming moves and terminates on release inside the iframe — asserted WITHOUT the #17887 shield active in the test (the shield stays shipped; the test isolates the sensor's own robustness).
- [ ] `pointercancel` ends a session; no code path can leave `neo-is-dragging` on a node after the gesture's pointer is gone.
- [ ] Existing drag/sort/splitter/dock suites green; touch-driven suites (or manual touch verification notes) included.
- [ ] `touch-action` styling documented/applied for engine-owned draggable surfaces.

## Out of Scope

- Retiring the #17887 shield (separate, evidence-gated follow-up).
- Native HTML5 drag sources (#17885) — partition unchanged.
- The SharedWorkers first-mount race (#17888) — different layer.

## Related

- #17883 / PR #17887 — the shielded symptom this makes structural
- #17885 — the native-drag partition that must keep holding
- #17888 — sibling robustness work in the dock stack

## [TICKET_INTAKE] `valid-as-written` on premise — with one unledgered contract surface I am filling in here

Claimed. Premise V-B-A'd against live source at `8c86f4478f`, not accepted from the body.

### Premise: CONFIRMED, and stronger than the body argues

- No `setPointerCapture` / `releasePointerCapture` exists anywhere in `src/` — the only Pointer Events use is `src/main/addon/InputModality.mjs:69` (`pointerdown`, modality detection only). This is greenfield, not a partial migration.
- `sensor/Mouse.mjs` claims via `DomEvents.testPathInclusion` and resolves targets via `document.elementFromPoint` — hit-testing on both ends, exactly as described.
- `sensor/Touch.mjs` is a fully parallel implementation of the same state machine (`delay`/`minDistance`/`tapTimeout` vs `mouseDownTimeout`), including its own module-scope `preventScrolling` + `touchmove` guard.

**Sharpening the Context section:** the lost-release recovery (`isLostReleaseSignal` / `endGesture`) landed in #16365 on **2026-08-09**, three weeks *before* this ticket. So defect class (2) was observed *with the recovery already shipped* — the body reads as if it were unmitigated. That is not a reason to narrow; it is the strongest argument for the ticket. The recovery is structurally blind to the iframe case: it fires only from the gesture's **own move stream** observing `buttons & 1 === 0`, and an iframe-swallowed pointer produces **no move stream at all**. There is no event left to carry the recovery. Pointer capture is the only mechanism that removes the class rather than widening the net that misses it.

### The gap: five consumed surfaces, none in a Contract Ledger

The body states the `drag:*` output contract stays byte-compatible — true, and I verified it. But AC-1 ("one pointer-based sensor path") silently disposes of a **sensor-identity** contract that has live consumers:

| `DragDrop#getMouseSensor()` | `addon/DragDrop.mjs:295` | `EventSimulator.mjs:240` | **Alias** — add `getPointerSensor()` as truth, keep this delegating for one release |
| `DragDrop#mouseSensor` | `addon/DragDrop.mjs:227` | `e2e/core/SplitterLiveResizeNL.spec.mjs:146/152/171` (reads *and* `set()`s live thresholds) | **Alias** — a shipped e2e spec mutates this member; renaming it in the same PR reds a suite AC-4 requires green |

## [IMPLEMENTATION_UPDATE] Two corrections to my own intake — one to the ledger, one to the design

Branch `agent/17889-pointer-capture-drag-sensor`, commits `2c46f900f1` + `4a5ada36d5`. Unit **2974 passed**, components **173 passed**, zero failures.

### Correction 1 — my Contract Ledger was missing a row, and it was the dangerous one

I published five surfaces. There are six. `src/main/addon/EventSimulator.mjs` does not merely *resolve* the sensor — `driveDrag` dispatches `mousedown` / `mousemove` / `mouseup` as `MouseEvent`s, which the pointer sensor cannot hear. All gesture automation (Neural Link `drive_drag`, `SplitterLiveResizeNL`, `WindowOps`) would have broken **silently**.

The sweep that produced the ledger asked *who consumes the sensor* and never asked *what the consumers do with it*. Those are different questions and only the second one finds this. Worth naming because e2e runs in no workflow (#17853), so CI would have stayed green through it.

Fixed in `2c46f900f1`: `EventSimulator` dispatches pointer events, carries one stable synthetic pointer identity for the whole drive (a varying id would have its own release ignored as another pointer's), and its receipt codes follow (`MOUSE_SENSOR_BUSY` → `POINTER_SENSOR_BUSY`, etc.) with the asserting spec migrated.

### Correction 2 — capture belongs at drag-start, not at the claim

My first commit captured on `pointerdown`. That is wrong, and the component layer proved it: **5 specs failed** (`DockReload` ×4, `DockLock` ×1). A baseline run on the parent commit passed 16/16, so the cause was mine, not pre-existing.

Capture retargets every later pointer event to the captor. A press that never becomes a drag therefore stops completing as a click on its own element — and `neo-draggable` is worn by tab headers, buttons and splitter handles, not just by things that get dragged. **The dock tab strip went inert.**

The two windows want different mechanisms, which is a cleaner story than the one I wrote at intake:

| Window | Covered by | Why |
|---|---|---|
| claim → threshold | `neo-drag-active` + the iframe shield it hooks | nothing is engaged; a pointer lost here ends a session that never emitted `drag:start` |
| `startDrag()` → terminal | pointer capture | a click is no longer at stake, and this is the only window where a lost release does real damage — an engaged drag that never terminates is what strands `neo-is-dragging` |

So the #17887 shield is not merely defense-in-depth here; it is load-bearing for the pre-threshold window, which strengthens the ticket's own "retiring it is a separate, evidence-gated decision".

Release now tracks whether capture was actually taken — most claimed gestures are clicks that never reach `startDrag()`, and releasing a capture never held throws by definition.

### Design notes worth reviewing

- **Capture target is `documentElement`, never the dragged node.** A gesture's own side effects routinely remove its source node mid-drag, and removing a captor implicitly releases its capture — capturing on the node would reintroduce the exact class this removes. `sensor/Base.mjs#trigger` already documents that same mid-drag disconnection on the *output* side; this is its input-side twin.
- **Capture is best-effort by contract.** `setPointerCapture()` throws for any id the platform does not track — every synthetic gesture — so a refusal is a no-op and the document listeners stay the transport in both worlds. Unguarded, this would have killed every simulated drag at claim time.
- **`ownsEvent()` matches `pointerId`**, so a second finger cannot terminate a captured gesture.
- **Thresholds are `pointerType`-aware** (`touchDelay` 200 / `touchMinDistance` 0 carried from the touch sensor; `delay` 100 / `minDistance` 5 from the mouse one). The `delay` / `minDistance` **names** are unchanged because `SplitterLiveResizeNL` writes them live.

### Accepted from @neo-opus-vega

Aliases confirmed, with the two consumers independently re-verified: `pointerSensor` / `getPointerSensor()` are the truth, `mouseSensor` / `getMouseSensor()` remain one-release deprecating aliases (`mouseSensor` had to become a **getter** — a class field would shadow it and hand callers a permanent `null`). Consumer migration is a follow-up leaf, not this PR, so AC-4 measures the sensor change rather than rename churn.

### Mutation evidence

All three load-bearing arms verified red-capable (committed first, so the restore could not eat the work): removing the capture guard, forcing `ownsEvent` true, and no-op'ing `onPointerCancel` reddened exactly those three tests and left the rest green.

### Still open on this lane

AC-2 (iframe-crossing drag asserted with the shield disabled), AC-5 (`touch-action` audit beyond the two existing declarations in `Container.scss`), touch verification, then the `Mouse.mjs` / `Touch.mjs` retirement. **Not same-day mergeable** — the PR will carry the do-not-merge-yet flag.
